title: India Nearly Missed the World Cup on Television. Zee Stepped In Ten Days Before Kickoff.
excerpt: After Reliance-Disney balked at FIFA's asking price and Sony walked away, Zee Entertainment secured an eight-year, $60 million deal that covers 39 FIFA events through 2034. Here is how to watch.
body:
For weeks, it looked like India — home to one of the world's fastest-growing football fanbases — might not be able to watch the 2026 FIFA World Cup at all. Negotiations between FIFA and the Reliance-Disney joint venture JioStar had stalled over a valuation gap so wide that Reuters reported it in early May. Sony held talks but walked away without making an offer. With the opening match in Mexico City just ten days out, India had no confirmed broadcaster.

Then, on June 1, Zee Entertainment stepped in.

The deal, finalised just ten days before kickoff, gives Zee the broadcast and streaming rights to the World Cup and 38 other FIFA events through 2034 — including the 2027 Women's World Cup in Brazil and the 2030 men's tournament in Spain, Portugal and Morocco. The price: approximately $60 million, a fraction of the $100 million FIFA had originally sought and considerably more than the $20 million Reliance-Disney had offered.

## How to Watch

For viewers in India, the tournament is available on Zee's newly launched Unite8 Sports network — Unite8 Sports 1 for Hindi commentary and Unite8 Sports 2 for English, both in HD. Digital viewers can stream every match live on the Zee5 app and website. The "All Access + Sports" three-month plan costs Rs 799 (roughly Rs 266 per month), enough to cover the entire tournament through the July 19 final.

Doordarshan's DD Sports will broadcast selected matches for free on television, including every quarterfinal, semifinal and the final — a crucial detail for the millions of Indian households that rely on free-to-air television.

## Cinema Screenings and Public Viewings

Zee has pushed the experience beyond living rooms. The company has partnered with PVR INOX and Cinepolis to screen select World Cup matches in cinemas across the country, offering fans a large-format viewing experience for marquee fixtures. Public viewing rights have also been awarded to Novex Communications, Eagles FC Kerala, Zion Bridge and What's up Goa, enabling authorised screenings at pubs, restaurants, clubs, gymkhanas, airports, hotels and educational institutions.

"In today's attention economy, shared experiences have become increasingly valuable, and live sports remain one of the few formats capable of bringing large audiences together in real time," said Gareth Eswin Thomas, Business Head of Zee Live.

## A Strategic Re-Entry

The deal marks Zee's return to sports broadcasting roughly eight years after it sold its sports assets to Sony. The market approved: Zee's shares jumped 6.4 per cent on the announcement. While cricket remains India's dominant sport, the youth demographic has shifted decisively toward global football, and Zee is now positioned to capture that audience for a decade.

## The NRI Angle

For NRIs in the United States, Canada and the UK — where the World Cup is being played or is in a convenient timezone — the broadcast deal has a different significance. Family back home can now watch the same tournament, at the same time, on their phones or televisions. Group chats that might have been one-sided ("Did you see that goal?") will now work both ways. The late-night and early-morning IST kickoff times remain a challenge, but at least the access problem has been solved.

Most matches in the US and Canada kick off between noon and 9 PM local time, which translates to 12:30 AM to 6:30 AM IST — a schedule that Indian football fans, long accustomed to staying up for Champions League matches, know well. The group stage runs through June 28, with the knockout rounds beginning July 1 and the final on July 19 at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey.
